description: An FP&A director must sign off on a twelve-million-dollar enterprise finance-system replacement and finalize its accounting treatment, fiscal-year funding split, and vendor payment protections, with input from accounting, treasury, and procurement.

shared_context.S1: The company is evaluating a finance-system replacement with a proposed total implementation budget of $12,000,000.
shared_context.S2: The board-approved capital-plan envelope can accommodate up to $12,000,000 for the project.
shared_context.S3: The vendor's implementation schedule runs from April through December of the current fiscal year.
shared_context.S4: Maya makes the final budget sign-off. At the weekly investment review, the accounting, treasury, and procurement owners each brief Maya on project conditions before she records the decision.

PF1.text: Jonas confirmed in an accounting memo received this morning that exactly 60% of the $12,000,000 project cost, or $7,200,000, meets the company's capitalization criteria; the memo has not yet been circulated to FP&A.

PF2.text: Leila's cash forecast review this week shows that only $9,000,000 can be funded before the end of the current fiscal year while preserving the approved minimum cash floor; the remaining $3,000,000 must be funded after October 1, and this forecast note has not yet been added to the investment packet.

PF3.text: Grant received the vendor's countersigned commercial schedule yesterday, requiring a 20% holdback on each implementation invoice until final acceptance; he has not yet uploaded the schedule to the procurement repository.

acceptance_conditions: The project must be approved with a total budget of exactly $12,000,000.
Exactly $7,200,000 of the budget must be classified as capitalized cost.
Exactly $9,000,000 must be funded during the current fiscal year.
Exactly $3,000,000 must be funded after October 1.
Each vendor implementation invoice must carry a 20% holdback until final acceptance.
The settlement must include accounting-treatment, staged-funding, and vendor-holdback commitments.
The current-fiscal-year funding must be released only while the approved minimum cash floor is maintained.
The accounting classification fact must be spoken by its owner and cited by Maya.

content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'cash_floor_gate' and c['target'] == 'current_fiscal_year_funding' and c['detail'] == 'release funding only while the approved minimum cash floor is maintained' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'accounting_treatment' and c['target'] == 'finance_system_replacement' and c['detail'] == 'capitalize exactly $7,200,000 of the $12,000,000 project budget' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] == 'staged_funding' and c['target'] == 'finance_system_replacement' and c['detail'] == '$9,000,000 in the current fiscal year and $3,000,000 after October 1' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any(c['type'] == 'vendor_holdback' and c['target'] == 'implementation_invoices' and c['detail'] == 'hold back 20% of each invoice until final acceptance' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The proposal gives no verified accounting split, while PF1 changes capitalized_cost_usd from an unspecified or generic full-expense treatment to exactly $7,200,000 and requires the accounting treatment to be recorded.

The April-to-December schedule does not establish affordable cash timing or a cash-floor safeguard, while PF2 changes the approval from an unsupported full-year funding plan to exactly $9,000,000 current_fiscal_year_funding_usd, exactly $3,000,000 post_october_funding_usd, and a minimum-cash-floor release condition.
The shared proposal contains no invoice protection, while PF3 changes vendor_holdback_percent from no specified holdback to exactly 20% on each implementation invoice.
